content.title: About
content.content: Tomatoes are the edible fruits of the tomato plant (Solanum lycopersicum), native to South America. They are now cultivated in warm regions worldwide and form the basis of many cuisines. Tomatoes have a juicy, slightly sweet‑tart flavor and a high water content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes belong to the nightshade family and are more closely related to potatoes than to vegetables.
There are over 10,000 tomato varieties, differing in color, shape, and taste.
The first tomatoes brought to Europe were thought to be poisonous because of their nightshade relatives.
Tomatoes are the main dietary source of lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that gives them their red color.
In 1893 the United States held its first contest for growing the largest tomatoes.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene has antioxidant properties and may help reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease and certain cancers.

items.title: Vitamins A and C
items.content: Tomatoes provide beta‑carotene (pro‑vitamin A) and vitamin C, which support immune function and skin health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A medium tomato contains about 20 kcal, making it an excellent choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports heart function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Tomato fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, ranging from skin rashes to swelling.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The high acidity of tomatoes can aggravate gastritis or heartburn in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Unwashed tomatoes may contain pesticide residues; it is advisable to rinse them thoroughly or choose organic varieties.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tomatoes can be eaten fresh in salads, sandwiches, and snacks, or used in sauces, soups, stews, and casseroles. They can be roasted, sautéed, or grilled. Consuming tomatoes with a small amount of fat improves lycopene absorption.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store tomatoes at room temperature, away from direct sunlight, to allow them to ripen. Ripe tomatoes are best used within 2–3 days; for longer storage they can be placed in the refrigerator, though this may affect texture.
